claims.text: Applying a TiO2 coating by sol-gel deposition can enhance the corrosion resistance of stainless steel in extreme environments.
The initial material is annealed AISI 304 stainless steel.
The surface modification consists of sol-gel deposition of a TiO2 coating.
The proposed TiO2 coating thickness is 500 nm.
The coated material is heat-treated at 500°C for 1 hour.
The intervention produces a TiO2 coating layer on the stainless-steel substrate.
The TiO2 layer acts as a barrier to penetration of corrosive species.
Blocking corrosive-species penetration reduces corrosion of the stainless-steel substrate.
The coating will reduce the corrosion rate by at least 70% relative to uncoated AISI 304 stainless steel.
The coated steel will have a corrosion rate below 0.1 mm/year.
Corrosion resistance may vary with deposition conditions, coating thickness, and heat-treatment parameters.
Corrosion performance can be evaluated by a 30-day immersion test in 3.5% NaCl at 25°C using uncoated AISI 304 as the control.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 70% corrosion-rate reduction, but the hypothesis is only falsified when the reduction is below 50%. An observed reduction between 50% and 70% would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
